reasoning: Hard gate fail on kelvin_ok. Failing reasons show BOTH cables stranded: /SENSEC1_HI, /SENSEC1_LO, /SENSEC2_HI, /SENSEC2_LO all have unconnected ratlines. The standing manager rule (rule 1) explicitly requires Kelvin stubs for failing cables before FR runs — but the directed stub summary exposes that rule is NOT being followed: compiled nets are [/CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA] with zero SENSEC* nets in the list and zero compile_failures. The stub compiler ran successfully and produced 7 stubs for control nets while silently omitting the Kelvin sense nets the rule targets. This is the operative failure: the rule exists but there is no enforcement gate that verifies the Kelvin stubs are actually present in the DSN before FR is launched. Additionally, gate_fail carries no direct scorer penalty — the gate failure cost is currently inferred only through kelvin_unrouted (1000) and drc (50), but if a future failure mode gates on a net type without its own metric key, there is no floor penalty. Adding a direct per-gate-fail penalty closes that gap and creates a steeper objective cliff separating any gate-failing candidate from a gate-passing one, regardless of secondary metric improvements. The new manager rule targets the enforcement gap demonstrated this round: a pre-flight cross-check that aborts if Kelvin stubs are missing, rather than silently proceeding with only control-net stubs compiled.

scorer_penalty.rationale: gate_fail currently has no penalty weight; each hard gate failure (kelvin_ok, diffpair_ok) produces gate_fail=1 but the only cost comes from per-metric penalties (kelvin_unrouted, drc). A direct 5000-per-gate-fail term creates a steep objective cliff ensuring any gate-failing candidate ranks far below any gate-passing candidate even if DRC and unconnected improve — and future gate types without their own metric key get penalized by default.

manager_rule: Before each FR run, cross-check the compiled stub nets list against every Kelvin net name appearing in failing_reasons; if any /SENSEC*_HI or /SENSEC*_LO net is present in failing_reasons but absent from the compiled stub nets, raise an explicit compile error and abort — do not launch FR until every failing Kelvin net has a locked stub at its shunt inner-edge pad coordinates. A missing Kelvin stub with no compile_failure entry is a silent mis-dispatch, not a pass.
